chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ma'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who left behind his mother and his brother. He said, 'O Shaykh, do you mean according to the Book (of Allah)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the nearest relative, then the nearest.' I said, 'Then the brother inherits nothing?' He said, 'I have told you that Ali (peace be upon him) used to give the wealth to the nearest relative, then the nearest.'

key_terms.الْكِتَابِ: the Book (referring to the Quran or established legal text)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed between a mother and a brother according to Imam Ali's practice?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia scholarly principle of *al-qarib fa al-qarib* (the closer first), illustrating how Imam Ali (AS) applied practical proximity alongside Quranic inheritance shares. It specifically addresses the scenario where a mother and brother are the sole heirs, establishing that the mother’s closer degree of kinship grants her precedence, thereby excluding the brother from receiving a share in this specific configuration. This narration is often cited to support the view that while the Quran sets fixed portions, the distribution among remaining heirs can be guided by the principle of closeness, a key distinction in Shia fiqh.
